clinicalPearls: An X-linked multisystem disorder affecting males, caused by loss-of-function variants in OCRL, which encodes a phosphatidylinositol phosphatase
Defined by a triad of eye, brain and kidney involvement: congenital cataracts, neurological impairment and a renal proximal tubulopathy
Congenital bilateral cataracts are present from birth and glaucoma may develop, so early ophthalmological assessment is essential
Neurological features include neonatal hypotonia, developmental delay, intellectual disability and, in some, behavioural problems and seizures
The kidney phenotype is a proximal (Fanconi-type) tubulopathy with low-molecular-weight proteinuria, aminoaciduria, phosphaturia, bicarbonate wasting and hypercalciuria
OCRL variants also underlie Dent disease 2, and the two conditions represent a phenotypic spectrum of the same gene
Female carriers are usually asymptomatic but may show characteristic lenticular opacities on slit-lamp examination
reference.pathophysiology: Lowe syndrome is caused by loss of function of OCRL, which encodes an inositol polyphosphate 5-phosphatase that regulates phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate at the Golgi, endosomes and primary cilium. Disrupted phosphoinositide metabolism impairs membrane trafficking, actin cytoskeletal organisation and endocytosis in multiple tissues. In the proximal tubule this compromises receptor-mediated endocytosis of filtered proteins, producing low-molecular-weight proteinuria and a generalised Fanconi-type tubulopathy; in the developing lens and brain the same trafficking defects lead to congenital cataract and neurodevelopmental impairment. The overlap with Dent disease 2 reflects a shared molecular basis with differing severity of extrarenal involvement.
additionalDifferentials: Cystinosis and other causes of renal Fanconi syndrome
Congenital infection causing cataract and neurological impairment
additionalInvestigations: Ophthalmological examination for congenital cataract and glaucoma
Assessment of proximal tubular function including low-molecular-weight proteinuria, aminoaciduria, phosphate, bicarbonate and urinary calcium
Developmental and neurological evaluation, with brain imaging where indicated
Serial kidney function and growth monitoring
Slit-lamp examination of the mother to detect carrier lens opacities
redFlags: Untreated congenital cataract threatening visual development, or rising intraocular pressure
Failure to thrive and growth failure from tubulopathy and acidosis
Seizures or significant electrolyte and acid-base disturbance
reference.prognosis: Lowe syndrome is a chronic multisystem condition; the proximal tubulopathy and, later, progressive chronic kidney disease, together with visual and neurodevelopmental impairment, determine outcome, and life expectancy is reduced though many survive into adulthood with supportive care.
pitfalls: Delaying cataract surgery and vision support, harming neurodevelopmental outcome
Failing to recognise and treat the Fanconi-type tubulopathy and its metabolic consequences
Not appreciating the OCRL spectrum linking Lowe syndrome and Dent disease 2
Overlooking carrier detection in the mother by slit-lamp examination
management: Correct the proximal (Fanconi) tubulopathy with alkali such as bicarbonate or citrate for the acidosis, oral phosphate and active vitamin D (calcitriol) for the phosphaturic bone disease, and potassium replacement
Arrange early cataract surgery for the congenital bilateral cataracts and lifelong ophthalmological monitoring and treatment of glaucoma
Provide neurodevelopmental support with physiotherapy, occupational and speech therapy, and treat seizures and behavioural problems as they arise
Monitor kidney function and growth serially and manage progressive chronic kidney disease, providing renal replacement therapy as it advances
Coordinate multidisciplinary care across nephrology, ophthalmology, neurology, clinical genetics and allied therapists
Offer genetic counselling for this X-linked disorder, with carrier testing of the mother including slit-lamp examination for lens opacities and cascade family screening
Escalate for acute metabolic derangement, uncontrolled glaucoma or declining renal function
